title: A boundary-sensitive and structure-adaptive lightweight network for medical image segmentation
content:
by Yaodong Guo, Yuzhu Liu, Sai Ma

Reliable medical image segmentation remains challenging in weak-contrast boundary regions, ambiguous anatomical transitions, and structurally heterogeneous areas. In addition, many high-performing models improve overlap-based metrics by introducing increasingly complex architectures, making it difficult to balance segmentation accuracy, boundary fidelity, and model compactness. To address these issues, this paper presents a boundary-sensitive and structure-adaptive lightweight framework for CT liver segmentation. The proposed method integrates three task-oriented components in a U-shaped architecture: Boundary-Sensitive Semantic Recalibration Attention (BSRA), Structure-Adaptive Scale Selection Fusion (SASF), and a Detail-Compensated Residual Lightweight Block (DCRB). Experiments were conducted on the CT subset of the CHAOS dataset under a patient-level five-fold cross-validation protocol. For each fold, metrics were first averaged across the corresponding test cases, and the reported values summarize the five fold-specific test means. Compared with the baseline U-Net, introducing BSRA increased Dice from 0.8443 to 0.8492 and improved Boundary F1-score from 0.7728 to 0.8081. The Boundary F1 improvement was statistically significant in the paired case-level Wilcoxon signed-rank test, whereas the Dice change was not significant, supporting the boundary-oriented role of BSRA. With the further incorporation of SASF, the performance-oriented variant achieved the best overall results, including a Dice coefficient of 0.8929, an Intersection over Union (IoU) of 0.8663, a Boundary F1-score of 0.8466, a 95% Hausdorff Distance (HD95) of 6.5729, and an Average Symmetric Surface Distance (ASSD) of 1.8947. After introducing DCRB, the lightweight variant still maintained competitive performance, attaining a Dice coefficient of 0.8710, an IoU of 0.8463, and a Boundary F1-score of 0.8392, while reducing the parameter count from 14.70M to 2.47M and the FLOPs from 31.81G to 8.44G. Additional validation on LiTS reproduced the same overall performance trends on a second liver CT dataset. These results show that the proposed framework improves region-level segmentation, boundary-level structural fidelity, and model compactness, providing a practical balance for CT liver segmentation.
